children: reaffirmed its full-year guidance Wednesday, citing continued momentum across its marine, nuclear and land operations as governments increase defense spending.

The British engineering and defense contractor said demand remained strong in its core markets. Babcock maintains the U.K. naval fleet, supplies weapons systems and provides engineering support for nuclear programs.

For investors, the update suggests Babcock is continuing to benefit from rising military budgets and growing demand for naval readiness, nuclear capabilities and defense infrastructure. Analysts surveyed by the company expect sales to reach £5.49 billion ($7.38 billion) in fiscal 2027, up from £5.19 billion a year earlier. Underlying operating profit is projected to rise to £464 million from £293 million.

The broader defense industry has seen an influx of orders as governments replenish equipment and respond to heightened geopolitical tensions, including the war with Iran. Larger British rival BAE Systems raised its 2026 profit forecast in July after reporting stronger demand.

Babcock also is awaiting more information about how the U.K. government will distribute its planned increase in defense investment. Britain outlined a £15 billion spending package in June that included £5 billion for drones and other autonomous systems, potentially creating additional opportunities for domestic contractors.

The company’s reaffirmed outlook indicates that current contracts and market demand remain sufficient to support its near-term targets. Further details on British defense spending could provide another catalyst if Babcock secures a meaningful share of new programs.

title: Babcock reaffirms outlook as defense and nuclear demand builds
